correctness.rationale: For R=k[y]/(y^n), write f=a+xb and let u,v be the valuations with zero assigned n. Then f²=a²+2xab, so square-zero means 2u≥n and, outside characteristic two, u+v≥n. The R-linear matrix of multiplication has equal diagonal a and sole off-diagonal b. If v≥u, eliminate b with a, leaving two factors of valuation u; if v<u, pivot on b and the other factor has valuation 2u−v capped at n. Zero factors give the same formula. The k-rank is therefore max(2(n−u),n−v), and m_f²=0 makes rank the number of Jordan blocks of size two. Every rank r is witnessed by xy^(n−r), including zero at r=0. Bounding rank gives u≥n−s and v≥n−r for s=floor(r/2), and 2u≥n is then automatic. In characteristic two these bounds give one linear space of dimension s+r. Outside characteristic two the spaces L_h in the proof exhaust all points: take h=n−u; conversely their defining inequalities imply square-zero and the rank bound. When s≤n−r they are nested. Otherwise the maximal ones are L_{n−r},…,L_s, of dimension n with intersection for i<j of dimension n−(j−i). The intersection with the previously added union is the intersection with the immediately preceding component, yielding q^n−q^(n−1) new points per step. This gives all cumulative counts including r=n. For e=r+s−n>0 these counts differ from q^(n+e) since q^e>1+e(1−1/q); the first such r is ceil(2(n+1)/3). The coefficient conditions and intersections apply over the algebraic closure and describe reduced support only. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed: it constructs finite multiplication matrices and compares Gaussian-elimination histograms with an equivalent valuation sum; it does not certify the universal geometric statement.
residual_risks: The recorded run on 18 finite configurations was not independently rerun; the general claim was checked algebraically. No assertion is made about the unreduced defining ideal.

originality.rationale: The distinct indexed all-element census for the exact same algebra gives the first and second power ranks on every valuation cell in positive characteristic and the corresponding finite-field weights. Selecting the cells with second power rank zero and first power rank at most r gives this census; taking their maximal closures yields exactly the reduced components. Equivalently, after the rank cutoffs the odd-characteristic region is a split-node jet locus with free tail coefficients, with an elementary coordinate-linear component rule. The extension to characteristic zero uses the same two formulas with 2 nonzero.
